To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Kupferschiefer in the study area was deposited in an euhaline (30–50‰) to mesohalene (30–40 ‰) water body with H2S-saturated bottom waters and a maximum water depth of 100 m.
the Zechstein sea water salinity was euhaline to slightly mesohaline and that the basin was anoxic to euxinic.
The Permian Kupferscheifer of the Lower Rhines Basin was deposited in a restricted marginal marine basin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the palaeoceanography, primary production, bacterial activity and the burial of organic matter in the Lower Rhines Basin during Kupferschief deposition.
the reconstruction of palaeoenvironments and the palaeoecology of the Kupferschiefer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Kupferschiefer represents a shallow water, euhaline to moderately brackish, anoxic (eauxinic) sea with high sulphate reduction rates and methanogenesis in the sediment.
the Zechstein sea was a shallow, euhaline to slightly mesohaline sea with a high primary production and a pronounced oxygen deficiency of the bottom waters.

the Kupferschiefer represents the remains of a shallow, brackish water environment, in which the water depth was restricted to a few tens of meters and the sediment consisted of anoxic (e.g., euxinic) muds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Lower Rhine Kupferschiefer basin was a shallow water basin, which was separated from the Zechstein sea by palaeohills.
the Lower Rhine basin was connected to the Zechstein sea during the Kupferschiefer event, but was isolated from it during most of the time of deposition of the overlying Upper Zechstein sediments.
the Zechstein sea water was euhaline to brackish, the bottom water anoxic and H2S-saturated and the sediment was characterised by high bacterial activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kupferschiefer shale in the study area was deposited in a small marginal basin of the Zechstein epicontinental sea.
the Zechstein basin was a shallow, euhaline to slightly brackish sea, with a high abundance of green/purple sulphurbacteria.
the Kupferschiefer in the Lower Rhines Basin was deposited in a brackish water environment with a maximum water depth of 100 m.
